q: 1. The activity which consumes maximum time is called
explain: The 'critical path' is the longest path, but a single activity consuming 'maximum time' is not a standard definition for a specific activity type in this context.

q: 2. A drawback of bar chart is
options: it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
all the activities represented are independent of each other
sequence of activities is not clearly defined
it is not possible to judge whether the activity is ahead or behind the schedule.
explain: The critical limitation of a standard bar chart is that it does not show logical dependency linkages or critical activity sequences.

q: 3. The number of post-activity associated with head event may be
explain: The final head event (end of project) has no subsequent activities (post-activities) following it.

q: 4. PERT is an abbreviation for
options: pertinent equation related to a task
explain: PERT stands for Program (Programme) Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 5. CPM stands for
explain: CPM stands for Critical Path Method, a network-based project scheduling technique.

q: 6. Latest finish time in CPM technique is indicated by
explain: Standard CPM notation uses rectangles (or squares) to denote time values like Latest Finish Time.

q: 7. When the times of earliest finish and the latest finish are equal in an operation, the operation is called
explain: If the earliest and latest times are equal, there is zero float, making that activity critical.

q: 8. An example for a parallel activity is
options: completing ground floor and starting first floor
wall and carpentry work of doors and windows
completion of flooring and initiating white washing
digging of a well and of septic tank
explain: Parallel activities can happen simultaneously; wall construction and carpentry can often proceed at the same time in different sections.

q: 9. A dummy activity
options: had no tail event but had only a head event
had only a head event but no tail event
does not require any resources or any time
had no sequence and can be fitted anywhere
explain: A dummy activity is a purely logical connection used to show dependency without adding time or cost to the project.

q: 10. Critical path is
options: shortest path for the earliest completion of the project
longest path of the network from the first event to the last event
ideal path by preceeding along which the project can be completed as per the schedule
the path which takes into account the completion of all the parallel activities
explain: The critical path is the specific sequence of activities that must be completed exactly as scheduled to finish the project on time.

q: 11. Which of the following is an example of parallel activities?
options: construction of walls and casting of roof
construction of walls and carpentry work of doors and windows
casting of roof and construction of parapet wall
digging of well and construction of septic tank
explain: Wall construction and carpentry (doors/windows) work can proceed simultaneously without one depending on completion of the other, making them parallel activities.

q: 12. The minimum number of critical path in a net work should be
explain: Every project network must have at least one critical path connecting the start to the end.

q: 13. Time and progress chart are also known as
explain: Per the answer key, d.

q: 14. Critical path network helps the engineer to
options: concentrate his attention on critical activitirs
divert the different resourced from non-critical activities to critical activities
be cautious for avoiding any delay in the critical activities
explain: CPM analysis allows engineers to focus on the most important tasks and manage resources across the project efficiently.

q: 15. The process of calculating the resources requirement of a project is known as
explain: Resource aggregation sums the resource requirement of all activities over time.

q: 16. In CPM, 'Forward Pass' and 'Backward Pass' are used to calculate respectively.
options: earliest expected time and latest allowable time
latest allowable time and earliest expected time
explain: Forward pass calculates Earliest times; Backward pass calculates Latest times.

q: 17. A dual role event
options: is the head event as well as a tail event
is the beginning of one event and the end of another
is any event other than the initial and final events
explain: A dual role event simultaneously serves as the head (completion) event of preceding activities and the tail (start) event of succeeding activities.

q: 18. The use of bar chart is very popular in construction department because
options: it is very simple to prepare and interpret
each item of work or activity is shown separately
modification to the chart, if required, can be carried out easily
explain: Bar charts are simple, show each activity separately and are easy to modify.

q: 19. A dummy activity
options: has no tail event but only a head event
has only head event but no tail event
does not require any resources or any time
has no bearing on the network and can appear anywhere
explain: A dummy activity is a fictitious link (zero duration, zero resource) used only to maintain logical sequencing between real activities.

q: 20. The constraints in case of resource smoothening operation would be
options: both resources and project duration time
explain: In smoothening the project duration is fixed, and resources are adjusted within it. Per the key, b.

q: 21. Positive float can occur when it is
explain: A sub-critical activity has a positive float, meaning it has extra time available and does not currently sit on the critical path.

q: 22. Negative float can occur when it is
explain: Negative float occurs in super-critical activities where the time required exceeds the time available, indicating the project is behind schedule.

q: 23. The estimated time required to complete an activity is termed as
explain: Duration is the standard term in project management for the estimated time needed to perform a specific task or activity.

q: 24. If the probability factor is zero, the chances of completing the project in scheduled time are;
explain: A probability factor (Z) of zero corresponds to the mean of the normal distribution, giving a 50% chance of completing within scheduled time.

q: 25. Free float is mainly used to
options: identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of preceeding activity
identify the activities, which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of either the preceeding or succeeding activities
explain: Free float is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting the earliest start time of any immediately following (succeeding) activities.

q: 26. In PERT, the critical path represents the
options: shortest path for the earliest completion of the project
longest path of the network from the initial to final event
ideal path by proceeding along which the project can be completed as per schedule
path which takes into account the completion of the parallel activities
explain: The critical path is defined as the longest path through the network from start to finish, determining minimum project duration.

q: 27. Whenever activity has zero total float, then
options: free float of the activity must be zero but independent float need not be zero
independent float must be zero but free float need not be zero
free float and independent float both must be zero
free float and independent float both need not be zero
explain: Since total float is the 'parent' float, if it is zero, all other sub-types of float (free and independent) must also be zero.

q: 28. Negative float for any activity means that the activity is:
explain: Negative float indicates the activity is behind schedule beyond what the project allows, making it super-critical (worse than critical).

q: 29. Area under beta distribution curve is divided into two equal parts by
explain: The expected time (mean of the beta distribution) divides the area under the probability distribution curve into two equal halves.

q: 30. Free float for any activity is defined as the difference between
options: its latest start time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest start time and earliest start time
its latest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its earliest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
explain: Free float is the Earliest Start of the successor minus the Earliest Finish of the current activity.

q: 31. The time by which a particular activity may be delayed without affecting the preceeding and succeeding activities is known as
explain: Independent float is unique because it doesn't affect the float of activities coming before or after it.

q: 32. Which of the following in a CPM network activity?
explain: In CPM, an 'activity' is an active process that consumes time and resources; 'excavation' is a clear action, while the others are often viewed as states/events.

q: 33. Which of the following terminology is not relevant to a CPM planning?
explain: Optimistic time is a PERT term (part of the three-estimate approach), not used in CPM which relies on single deterministic durations.

q: 34. Gnatt chart indicates
options: balance of work to be done
comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: A Gantt chart compares actual progress against the schedule.

q: 35. According to Fulkerson's, the correct event numbers corresponding to event A, B, C, D, E of the network shown in figure
explain: Fulkerson's Rule (I-J numbering) requires that the number at the head of an arrow is always greater than the number at the tail.

q: 36. Actual performance of a task is called
explain: An activity represents the actual performance of work/task in a project.

q: 37. On a bar chart the various activities of a project are shown by
explain: Each activity is a horizontal bar drawn against the time scale.

q: 38. A fictious activity with zero duration and no cost used to maintain the sequential order of the activities in network is known as a
explain: A dummy activity is a logical link represented by a dashed arrow that consumes no time or resources.

q: 39. Zero float for any activity means that the activity is
explain: Zero float (zero slack) means the activity has no spare time and lies exactly on the critical path, making it critical.

q: 40. Jobs going ahead of schedule are conveniently shown in
explain: Per the answer key, Gantt chart.

q: 41. Earliest finish time of an activity is always
options: equal to or more than earliest event
equal to or less than earliest event time of the following node
more than earliest time of the following node
explain: The finish time of an activity must occur by the time the following node (event) is reached; it cannot exceed that event's earliest time.

q: 42. Positive float for any activity means that the activity is
explain: Positive float indicates the activity has spare time available and can be delayed without affecting the project, making it sub-critical.

q: 43. The weakness in bar chart is
options: uncertainty in duration for various activities
the sequence of activities is not very clear
explain: Bar charts do not show interdependencies, uncertainty or clear sequence.

q: 44. Latest start of activity is always
options: less than or equal to latest event time of preceeding node
more than or equal to latest events time of preceeding node
equal to latest event time of preceeding node
explain: The latest an activity can start must be at or after the latest time its preceding event (node) can occur.

q: 45. A milestone chart
options: shows the interdependence of various jobs
shows the events in chronological, but not in a logical sequence
explain: Milestone charts list events in time order without showing logical links.

q: 46. Latest start time is the
options: latest time by which an activity can be started without delaying the project
latest time by which an activity can be completed without delaying the project
latest time the event can occur
explain: Latest Start Time (LST) is the maximum delay possible for the start of a task that won't push back the project completion date.

q: 47. The interrelationship between the functional elements of a programme is achieve through
explain: A work breakdown structure shows how the elements of a programme relate.

q: 48. If a is the optimistic time, b is the pessimistic time and m is the most likely time, then the average time is equal to
explain: The formula for expected (average) time in a Beta distribution is t_e = (a + 4m + b) / 6.

q: 49. The difference between the total float and the free float is termed as
explain: Interfering float is the difference between Total Float and Free Float (TF - FF).

q: 50. An event is
options: a definite position of an activity
explain: Per the answer key, d. An event is an instant at which activities start or finish.
